subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron output-target contract, and if so which targets and failure semantics should be part of the core API?
rationale: The request crosses config/schema, framework-owned file writes, channel fan-out, session-state injection, and failure reporting, so implementation cannot safely choose the product and security contract by inference.

options.title: Design the full output contract
options.body: Specify the core schema, target authorization rules, status/fallback model, and migration/docs expectations before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to session delivery first
options.body: Keep this broad issue open as design context but land only a smaller `delivery.mode="session"` or session-target follow-up after maintainer approval.

options.title: Reject core output fan-out
options.body: Leave cron output routing to prompts, tools, webhooks, or plugins and close the broad core feature after an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design the full output contract
recommendation.body: Specify the core schema, target authorization rules, status/fallback model, and migration/docs expectations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show active work on cron delivery routing and docs, and the decision spans product/security boundaries rather than a single implementation seam.
